title: ITY and ETY
kidRule: Lots of naming words end with the sound 'ih-tee'. It is nearly always spelled I-T-Y, as in ACTIVITY. But right after the letter I we write E-T-Y instead, as in VARIETY, so that two I's never bump together!
hint: This naming word ends with a sound like 'ih-tee'. Look at the letter just before the ending. Is it an I?
reminder: The ending is I-T-Y, unless the letter just before it is an I. Then it is E-T-Y.

check.question: Why does VARIETY end with E-T-Y and not I-T-Y?
check.correctAnswer: Because there is already an I just before the ending, so E-T-Y is used instead!
distractors: Because long words always end with E-T-Y
Because a word that starts with V can never end with I-T-Y

words.def: Something that you do, often for fun or to learn.
words.sent: My favorite rainy-day activity is building a blanket fort.
words.story: Doctors say that children should get at least 60 minutes of physical activity every day, and running, dancing, and climbing all count!
words.card: For today's *activity*, we will *act* like penguins at a pool party!

words.def: A lot of different kinds of things.
words.sent: The bakery sells a variety of muffins.
words.story: More than 7,500 different kinds of apples are grown around the world!
words.card: My sock drawer has a *variety* of colors, and *vari*ous holes too!

words.def: The pull that makes things fall down toward the ground.
words.sent: The apple fell from the tree because gravity pulled it down.
words.story: The Moon's gravity is only about one sixth as strong as the Earth's, so on the Moon you could jump about six times higher!
words.card: The *grav*y slid off my plate, and I blame *gravity*!

words.def: All the people who live together in a place and share its rules; also a club for people who like the same thing.
words.sent: A fair society takes care of all its people.
words.story: Ants live in a society too! Each ant has a job, such as nurse, builder, or food finder.
words.card: The ant *society* was *so* busy that nobody noticed the picnic was over!

words.def: A kind of energy that flows through wires and makes lights and machines work.
words.sent: The storm knocked out the electricity, so we used flashlights.
words.story: An electric eel makes its own electricity, and a big one can give a zap of more than 600 volts!
words.card: The whole *city* cheered when the hamster wheel made enough *electricity* for one night-light!

words.def: A strong wish to know or learn about something.
words.sent: Her curiosity led her to ask how rainbows are made.
words.story: NASA's Curiosity rover has been exploring Mars since 2012. A sixth-grade student named Clara Ma chose its name!
words.card: The *curiosity* of Ma*rio* the mouse got him stuck in the cookie jar!

words.def: The amount of water in the air, which can make a day feel sticky.
words.sent: The humidity in the rain forest made my hair curl.
words.story: When the humidity is high, the sweat on your skin cannot dry quickly, and that is why a damp day feels hotter!
words.card: In the *mid*dle of the jungle, the *humidity* turned my hair into a bird's nest!

words.def: A good chance to do something.
words.sent: The field trip was a great opportunity to see real dinosaur bones.
words.story: NASA's Opportunity rover was built to work on Mars for about 90 days, but it kept going for more than 14 years!
words.card: At the air*port*, I had the *opportunity* to high-five a pilot!

words.def: Being happy to give and share with others.
words.sent: Thanks to her generosity, everyone at the table got a cookie.
words.story: Scientists have found that giving to other people makes the giver feel happier too!
words.card: With great *generosity*, the *gen*tle giant shared his giant sandwich!

words.def: A feeling of cheerful fun and happiness.
words.sent: The room was full of gaiety, with music, balloons, and laughter.
words.story: The Gaiety Theatre in Dublin, Ireland, opened in 1871, and people still go there to watch shows today!
words.card: The sn*ai*l parade filled the garden with *gaiety*, very slowly!
